meta.title: Herdr Power Keys — Keyboard Field Guide
meta.description: A verified, glanceable keyboard field guide for moving through Herdr tabs, panes, workspaces, and power-user controls.

props.title: Drive Herdr without touching the mouse
props.subtitle: One prefix. One follow-up key. Tabs, panes, workspaces, and agent terminals at full speed.
props.meta: Verified against the locally installed Herdr default configuration · July 17, 2026

props.content: Your immediate answer: **next tab is `Ctrl+B`, release, then `N`**. Previous is `Ctrl+B`, then `P`. Jump directly with `Ctrl+B`, then `1` through `9`.

props.title: Change tabs
props.subtitle: Herdr uses a tmux-style prefix sequence, not one giant chord.

export.title: Herdr tab switching
export.markdown:
### Change tabs
- Next: Ctrl+B, then N
- Previous: Ctrl+B, then P
- Direct: Ctrl+B, then 1 through 9
- New: Ctrl+B, then C

props.title: Release the prefix
props.content: Press **Ctrl+B**, release both keys, then press the action key. You are not meant to hold `Ctrl+B` while pressing `N`, `P`, or a number. If you get lost, press `Esc` and start again.

props.label: THE WHOLE MENTAL MODEL
props.title: Prefix → action → back to work
props.subtitle: This is sequencing, not advanced Vim.

props.title: 1 · Arm Herdr
props.content: Press `Ctrl+B`. Herdr now waits for one command key instead of sending that key to the terminal pane.

props.title: 2 · Choose the action
props.content: Press `N`, `P`, `1…9`, `H/J/K/L`, or another mapped key. Uppercase actions mean hold `Shift` for the second key.

props.title: 3 · Keep typing
props.content: Herdr executes once and immediately returns keyboard control to the focused terminal. No persistent Vim mode to remember.

props.label: CORE MAP
props.title: Tabs and workspaces
props.subtitle: Learn the six tab keys first. Workspace controls can wait until tab movement is automatic.

props.label: PANE CONTROL
props.title: Move and reshape the terminal
props.subtitle: The H/J/K/L keys are positional: left, down, up, right.

props.title: Focus by direction
props.content:
`Ctrl+B → H/J/K/L`

Left · down · up · right. Think of `J` as falling down and `K` as climbing up.

props.title: Cycle panes
props.content:
`Ctrl+B → Tab`

Reverse with `Ctrl+B → Shift+Tab`. Useful when the visual direction is ambiguous.

props.title: Vertical split
props.content:
`Ctrl+B → V`

Creates a side-by-side pane split.

props.title: Horizontal split
props.content:
`Ctrl+B → -`

Creates a pane above/below the current pane.

props.title: Zoom focused pane
props.content:
`Ctrl+B → Z`

Toggle the active pane between normal layout and fullscreen.

props.title: Resize mode
props.content:
`Ctrl+B → R`

Enter resize controls when the split proportions are wrong.

props.title: Close pane
props.content:
`Ctrl+B → X`

Closes only the focused pane—not the whole tab.

props.title: Toggle sidebar
props.content:
`Ctrl+B → B`

Recover screen space, then toggle it back when you need the agent queue.

props.label: POWER MOVES
props.title: Use visual navigation while Vim muscle memory catches up
props.subtitle: You can be fast before H/J/K/L feels natural.

props.title: Go To navigator
props.content: Press `Ctrl+B → G`, then use the **arrow keys** to move through the navigation surface. Herdr also accepts `H/J/K/L` there, so you can introduce Vim motion gradually instead of memorizing it under pressure.

props.title: Leave unbound features unbound
props.content: Previous/next workspace, previous/next agent, direct agent focus, and open/remove worktree have no default shortcut. That is deliberate. Bind them only after a repeated workflow proves you need them.

props.label: 10-MINUTE MUSCLE-MEMORY DRILL
props.title: Learn in layers
props.subtitle: Do not memorize the whole sheet at once.

props.title: Stage 1 · Tabs
props.content: Create three tabs with `Ctrl+B → C`. Cycle five times with `N`, reverse with `P`, then jump directly using `1`, `2`, and `3`. Stop here until this feels boring.

props.title: Stage 2 · Panes
props.content: Make one vertical split with `V` and one horizontal split with `-`. Move using `H/J/K/L`, toggle zoom with `Z`, then cycle with `Tab`.

props.title: Stage 3 · Workspaces
props.content: Open the workspace picker with `W`, then open Go To with `G`. Use arrows first. Add Vim movement only after the navigation model is obvious.

props.label: RECOVERY KEYS
props.title: When you forget
props.subtitle: The best power-user shortcut is the one that teaches you the others.

props.title: Open the shortcut help
props.content:
`Ctrl+B → ?`

Use Herdr's own help overlay as the authoritative live map. It reflects the running version and any custom bindings.

props.title: Session controls
props.content:
`Ctrl+B → S` settings

`Ctrl+B → Shift+R` reload config

`Ctrl+B → Q` detach from the persistent session

`Ctrl+B → O` open notification target

props.title: Tabs are also scriptable
props.subtitle: Useful when you want shell aliases or agent-driven workspace control.
